title: Hot/Warm/Cold Tiering
description: Moves objects between Standard, Infrequent Access, and Glacier tiers by age and access count. Hot data stays on fast storage; untouched data sinks to cheap tiers automatically. The policy is the product: most cloud storage bills drop 40 to 70 percent with sane tiering.
key_mechanisms: Classify objects by age and access heat
Restore quickly when cold data heats up

demo.title: Demo — Hot/Warm/Cold Tiering

title: Lifecycle Policy Engines
description: Applies declarative rules that transition objects on age, version count, or tags. Instead of scripts, operators write policies like 'move to cold after 90 days, delete after 7 years' and the engine enforces them. Policies are versioned and auditable.

demo.title: Demo — Lifecycle Policy Engines

title: Hierarchical Storage Management
description: Transparently migrates files between SSD, disk, and tape via stub files that recall data on access. Applications see a normal filesystem while HSM moves the bytes behind the scenes. It brings mainframe-era tiering to modern NAS.
key_mechanisms: Stage files to fast tiers on access
Migrate idle files to slow tiers

demo.title: Demo — Hierarchical Storage Management

title: Compaction-Driven Migration
description: Uses LSM compactions to rewrite cold SSTables into cheaper storage classes as a side effect of normal maintenance. The compaction job already rewrites the data; pointing cold levels at cheap storage makes tiering nearly free. It couples the storage engine's write path to the tiering policy.
key_mechanisms: Map LSM levels to storage classes
Rewrite cold levels to cheap storage
Keep hot levels on fast media

demo.title: Demo — Compaction-Driven Migration

title: Age-Based Archival
description: Archives records older than the retention threshold to immutable storage. Financial, medical, and legal records have mandated retention periods; archival jobs move them to WORM storage when they age out of active use. Retrieval is slower but compliance is automatic.
key_mechanisms: Define retention thresholds per record class
Move aged records to immutable storage

demo.title: Demo — Age-Based Archival

title: Access-Frequency Promotion
description: Promotes frequently-read cold objects back to hot tiers automatically. Tiering is not one-way: when an old object goes viral, the promoter moves it up before users feel the latency. Promotion thresholds prevent flapping on borderline objects.

demo.title: Demo — Access-Frequency Promotion

title: Deduplication Tiers
description: Stores deduplicated chunks on capacity tiers while hot metadata stays on flash. Chunk-level dedup finds repeated data across files, and only unique chunks consume capacity. It is how backup systems store petabytes affordably.

demo.title: Demo — Deduplication Tiers

title: Erasure Coding Transitions
description: Converts replicated hot data to erasure-coded cold storage, cutting overhead from 3x to about 1.4x. Triple replication is fast but wasteful; erasure coding trades some repair cost for major capacity savings. The transition happens as data cools.

demo.title: Demo — Erasure Coding Transitions

title: Snapshot Lifecycle
description: Ages volume snapshots into archive tiers and prunes expired ones on schedule. Snapshots accumulate silently and expensively; lifecycle rules move old ones to cheap storage and delete what retention no longer requires. It is basic hygiene with real money attached.

demo.title: Demo — Snapshot Lifecycle

title: WORM Compliance Tiers
description: Locks regulated records in write-once-read-many tiers with legal-hold policies. Once written, the data cannot be altered or deleted until retention expires — even by administrators. It satisfies regulators who require tamper-evident retention.

demo.title: Demo — WORM Compliance Tiers

title: Cost-Aware Placement
description: Places each object where cost per GB-month is minimized given its access pattern. The placer solves a small optimization: storage price plus expected retrieval fees, per object, per region. It beats static tiering when access patterns vary widely.
key_mechanisms: Assign each object to the cheapest fit

demo.title: Demo — Cost-Aware Placement

title: Geo-Tiering
description: Keeps hot copies near users and cold copies in the cheapest region. Latency-sensitive data lives at the edge; archival copies sit where storage is cheapest. The system routes reads to the nearest hot copy and never pays edge prices for cold bytes.
key_mechanisms: Replicate hot data to user regions
Route reads to the nearest copy

demo.title: Demo — Geo-Tiering

title: Media Refresh Cycles
description: Rewrites aging tapes and disks before media end-of-life to prevent bit rot from becoming data loss. Every medium has a rated lifespan; refresh jobs copy data to fresh media on schedule and verify every byte. It is unglamorous and essential.
key_mechanisms: Track media age against rated lifespan
Copy to fresh media on schedule

demo.title: Demo — Media Refresh Cycles

title: Migration Verification
description: Checksums every migrated object against the source before deleting originals. Migration without verification is data loss with extra steps; the verifier compares strong hashes end to end. Only verified objects are released from the source tier.

demo.title: Demo — Migration Verification

title: Zero-Downtime Rebalancing
description: Moves shards between storage classes without pausing reads or writes. Dual-read and write-shadowing keep the shard available while bytes move underneath. Cutover is atomic, and rollback is a routing change away.

demo.title: Demo — Zero-Downtime Rebalancing
